target_customer: Large specialty farms and growers that employ seasonal field labor
problem: Growers struggle to track worker time, harvest piece rate productivity and labor compliance on paper.
product_category: Agricultural workforce and harvest management software

founders.name: Harrison Steed
founders.background_notes: Grew up working on the family blueberry, avocado and citrus farm in Southern California and wrote software for problems they faced (igrownews).

founders.name: Austin Steed
founders.background_notes: Brother of Harrison; same farm background.

technical_complexity.rationale: Time tracking and harvest data capture on mobile devices for farms is mostly standard application work.

defensibility.rationale: Payroll and compliance integrations create lock in with growers over time, but the early product was simple.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquirer; Terminus Capital Partners took a majority stake in October 2026 and the founders stayed.

market_need_then: Founders lived the labor tracking problem on a family farm; large farms face piece rate pay and labor compliance rules (company story via igrownews).

brand_strength.rationale: Known in the specialty crop niche; no press about the brand itself found.

outcome_analysis: PickTrace started as a labor tool built by brothers who grew up on a family farm, then expanded into onboarding, payroll, compliance and quality control for specialty growers. Funding stayed small and mostly undisclosed, and it took a majority investment from Terminus Capital Partners in October 2026, which suggests a steady niche software business.
notes: CB Insights (aggregator, placeholder amounts) lists 2015 seed rounds with FundersClub and YC and a 2018 Series A with undisclosed investors; unverified so not recorded as rounds.
